title: Riley Wheel Brawl: 500 proposed future improvements
id_policy: Stable F001–F500 IDs. Proposed P01–P10 batches are not release versions or commitments.

effort_legend.S: A contained change in one subsystem or a small authored asset set.
effort_legend.M: Several coordinated changes or a substantial content asset.
effort_legend.L: A new system, complex interaction, large authored set or cross-device validation effort.

priority_legend.P1: Foundation, player safety/readability, compatibility or required acceptance gate.
priority_legend.P3: Optional polish or experiment to select after feedback.

dependency_policy: An empty dependencies array means no prerequisite among these 500 items, not exemption from existing release gates. Dependencies may be scheduled earlier than their batch when needed; do not waive acceptance to complete a batch.
guardrails: The present 50-item 1.1 deliverable and its unresolved evidence gates take precedence; this roadmap does not delay it or claim its completion.
All 500 entries are proposed future work, not built features, approved release scope or a promise to implement everything.
Keep painted art, the no-build browser runtime, offline single-player play, Riley age 16 with blue glasses and sleeveless black coat, and TT age 8 with her blue dancer identity.
No accounts, public leaderboards, tracking, monetization, paid services, voice cloning or routine external transmission. Proposed statistics and profiles remain local and user-controlled.
New recorded assets remain optional, locally available, versioned and backed by existing procedural or synthesized fallbacks; real listening and art review remain necessary.
Creative approvals and required licenses must be resolved before producing or distributing new material. New terms, downloads, permission grants or external sharing require their applicable approval.
New assisted settings are labeled and excluded from standard Normal/Hard balance and strict real-time performance evidence. Never slow a clock to pass a standard gate.
The original five-stage Normal and Hard matrix remains separate from remix and expansion matrices. New content must not silently change those five stage configurations.

Exactly two optional new levels are proposed. Exactly one optional additional cinematic reel per original stage is proposed in F151–F155; galleries, captions, static postcards and environmental vignettes add no further reels.
Preserve inherited tests and protected source art. Any genuine contract conflict needs an explicit review decision, not a quietly weakened threshold.
Browser simulation and automated playthroughs do not certify physical hardware, actual listening or voluntary family playtests. Mark blocked or unrun gates honestly.
Select and review each batch before implementation; publish only after fresh explicit GO for the exact reviewed candidate.

original_five_stage_balance_policy.normal: Retain the current V11_PLAN.md requirement: each stage within five percentage points of freshly measured live 1.0 using the unchanged reference protocol.
original_five_stage_balance_policy.hard: Retain the current V11_PLAN.md late-stage targets for S3/S4/S5 of 50/35/25 percent and report all five stages under the locked reference protocol.
original_five_stage_balance_policy.separation: Remix, practice, assistance and optional-level results are separate reports; none may substitute for any original-stage result.

passes.title: Access and reading comfort
passes.rationale: Make the game easier to read and operate before asking players to learn more systems. Assisted variants stay visibly separate from standard balance and performance results.

passes.title: Practice and skill discovery
passes.rationale: Provide a safe place to learn the current game, test access choices and understand mistakes before expanding combat complexity.

passes.title: Optional combat remix
passes.rationale: Put new enemies, techniques and encounter rules behind a separate remix route so the original five-stage experience retains its measured identity.

passes.title: Family story and chapter replay
passes.rationale: Deepen the existing rescue story through optional short scenes, readable context and spoiler-aware replay rather than extending the main rescue plot.

passes.title: Painted presentation assets
passes.rationale: Add authored painted objects, effects and selective character animation after gameplay needs are clear; keep approved source paintings intact.

passes.title: Sound character and mix choice
passes.rationale: Add original or suitably licensed offline sound detail and per-category control; preserve the existing theme and make all alternate music optional.

passes.title: Broader device and control support
passes.rationale: Extend beyond standard-controller and basic-touch support with explicit local profiles, calibration, hybrid input and browser-aware controls.

passes.title: Offline ownership and resilience
passes.rationale: Make longer-term play safer with verified offline packs, local backups, recovery paths and bounded resource lifetimes.

passes.title: Authoring and review tools
passes.rationale: Reduce the cost of safely maintaining a larger game through reusable local editors, deterministic evidence and content validation.

passes.title: Two optional post-finale levels
passes.rationale: Add River Docks and Mountains of Mist only after the core is stable; give each its own targets, evidence and release decision.

items.improvement: Offer a first-run access setup card
items.acceptance: A skippable card previews text, motion and controls; skipping leaves the current defaults and can be reopened from Options.

items.improvement: Scale dialogue independently of the HUD
items.acceptance: Three caption sizes keep the complete longest line readable without covering Riley's combat lane at 640x360.

items.improvement: Add a bundled easy-reading text face
items.acceptance: Players can choose a locally bundled proportional face for prose while labels remain aligned and font loading works offline.
With manual advance enabled, every reel caption remains until deliberate confirm, including after audio ends.
Turning typing off displays the complete caption on its first frame without advancing the story or interrupting its voice.
At minimum and maximum opacity, caption text remains legible on the brightest Tear and darkest Shadar Logoth samples.
Each speaker has a named, distinct geometric marker that is recognizable when portraits and color are unavailable.

items.improvement: Choose top or bottom dialogue placement
items.acceptance: The two caption placements respect reserved HUD regions and remember the choice across story and combat dialogue.
A read-only log contains the last 30 heard lines with speaker names; opening it pauses play and never reveals future lines.
Full meter, healing, incoming ranged attacks and Loial arrival receive distinct optional text cues when dialogue is absent.
Offscreen threat captions include left or right based on world position, updating correctly as the camera moves.
The preset enables essential captions and visual readiness cues; a muted five-stage playthrough requires no sound-only decision.
Mono combines both channels without clipping; every left-only and right-only test cue is audible through either output channel.
Rumble can be disabled without changing music or effects, and no actuator request occurs while that setting is off.
The new option removes shake, punch and cinematic pans while preserving hit timing, screen coverage and stage navigation.
Super, damage and lightning visuals use a restrained alternate treatment while their warning and damage intervals remain unchanged.

items.improvement: Show taint with a static warning alternative
items.acceptance: A patterned border and countdown convey grace, warning and damage phases without wobble or pulsation.

items.improvement: Allow ambient background animation to stop
items.acceptance: Snow, pennants and decorative movement can freeze while enemies, hazards and all gameplay cues continue normally.
Light and dark outline styles preserve painted interior pixels and make Riley identifiable against five representative backgrounds.
Mashadar, fire and beam warnings use different pattern shapes that remain distinguishable in grayscale at the 640x360 gameplay size.
Healing, angreal and saidin markers remain distinct at small size without relying on blue, orange or yellow differences.
An optional countdown matches the remaining grace period within one simulation tick and pauses with gameplay.
A keyboard or menu action reads the current HP, lives, saidin and Loial availability from a semantic text region.

items.improvement: Mirror menu choices into semantic controls
items.acceptance: Title, Options, pause and outcomes expose named, operable buttons in an accessibility tree with no duplicate activation.

items.improvement: Show a consistent semantic focus indicator
items.acceptance: Keyboard focus is visible on every mirrored control and stays on the invoked row when returning from a subpanel.

items.improvement: Announce scene changes to assistive readers
items.acceptance: Entering title, a stage, pause or an outcome produces one concise announcement; regular frames produce none.
Repeated identical low-health and meter notices produce at most one announcement per state change while manual status remains available.
Every existing story plate has a brief selectable description that conveys the scene without spoiling later captions.
At 200% text size, semantic menus reflow without horizontal scrolling and every action remains reachable at a 320px CSS width.
Selected, disabled and ordinary rows remain distinguishable by border or shape in both high-contrast palette variants.
Dialogue and explanations can use sentence case while names, button bindings and saved content retain their correct meaning.
Three previewable palettes alter cue colors only; grayscale and representative color-vision simulations retain each cue's shape distinction.

items.improvement: Allow the status HUD to move to either upper corner
items.acceptance: HP and meter panels can swap corners without overlapping captions, boss bars or the pause control.

items.improvement: Add a temporary Find Riley marker
items.acceptance: A freely bound locator displays above Riley for one second, follows jump height, and costs no gameplay resource.
Only foreground scenery in front of Riley becomes locally translucent; enemy visibility and collision remain unchanged.
An optional timed scan highlights one semantic menu action at a time; one switch selects it, a dedicated escape target is always reachable, and gameplay never auto-activates.

items.improvement: Offer hold-to-repeat basic kicks as an assist
items.acceptance: Holding kick issues ordinary legal kick presses only; assisted runs are labeled and excluded from unchanged Normal/Hard comparison data.
With this optional aid on, an attack press faces the nearest eligible target in reach only when no direction is held; hitboxes stay unchanged and the run is labeled assisted.
Opt-in targeting adjusts only within a documented small lane angle, never selects behind Riley, and labels the run assisted.

items.improvement: Add an explicitly assisted slow-play mode
items.acceptance: A 75% or 90% simulation-speed choice also slows tells and hazards; records show the speed and never count toward standard pacing or balance gates.
Only assisted runs may double the grace interval; save/resume preserves the selected multiplier and Standard remains byte-for-byte configured as before.

items.improvement: Bind spin to a separate optional action
items.acceptance: A dedicated remappable spin action performs the same move as down-plus-kick and does not consume another action on the same edge.

items.improvement: Offer toggle movement for motor access
items.acceptance: An opt-in direction latch stops on opposing direction, pause or explicit stop; returning from a menu never resumes latched motion.

items.improvement: Mirror touch controls for left-handed play
items.acceptance: A single previewed switch exchanges stick and action clusters while preserving labels and safe-area margins.
Three touch sizes maintain nonoverlapping active regions or clearly explain the layout limit before applying.
Players can place each control inside a safe preview area, undo changes and restore defaults without spending a combat action.
The setting visibly previews the activation area, clamps to the safe region and remains independent of movement speed.

items.improvement: Add optional dwell selection for menus
items.acceptance: A visible dwell timer activates one focused menu row, cancels when focus moves and never applies to gameplay or destructive actions.

items.improvement: Explain access options in plain language
items.acceptance: Each option has one short purpose statement and names any assisted-run effect; reading the guide changes no settings.
Applying a preset stores the previous settings until confirmed; cancellation restores all changed values together.
The title opens a separate no-score training scene whose exit returns to title without overwriting campaign Continue.
A dummy can stand, guard or move in a chosen lane; changing its behavior resets only its local exercise state.
Reset restores Riley, target, pickups, camera and exercise counters to the selected drill's start in under one second.
A paused drill advances exactly one simulation tick per step and shows that frame stepping is unavailable in campaign.
An optional ten-entry history distinguishes press, hold and release and uses the player's current binding labels.
Startup, active and recovery bands match the selected move's actual state on every stepped frame.
Hit, hurt and lane-depth volumes are separately labeled and disappear completely on leaving practice without changing collision outcomes.

items.improvement: Explain practice damage and meter gains
items.acceptance: Each hit reports base damage, modifiers and saidin gained; displayed sums match the target's state delta.
A local ten-second attempt replay reproduces inputs and outcomes from its starting snapshot without changing campaign randomness.
A drill passes only after front, roundhouse and back kick connect in order and points out the first mistimed link.
Three marked approach distances distinguish too far, correct reach and overshoot using the actual airborne collision result.
A target in a neighboring lane cannot pass the exercise until Riley aligns and lands a valid hit.
The exercise records a launch followed by an airborne hit and explains when a second hit arrives after landing.

items.improvement: Teach grab, knee and throw choices
items.acceptance: A practice target supports each existing grab branch; the checklist completes only after three distinct legal outcomes.
The player lands three spaced shots; an early press is identified as cooldown rather than a missed target.
A hovering target must be struck at two heights; the exercise shows the release-time aim direction before retry.
A three-target arrangement can be hit by one empowered spread and reports which projectile hit each target.
A refillable drill reaches full meter, shows the grace period and succeeds when super is spent before the first taint tick.
Two formations demonstrate aligned and misaligned calls; reset restores training Loial without altering campaign availability.
A practice boss survives a super and displays exact HP removed, demonstrating that screen-clear behavior differs for ordinary enemies.
A side-by-side training readout uses identical targets with and without Callandor and reports the measured damage difference.
A drill distinguishes protected recovery from the first vulnerable frame and rewards moving to a clear lane afterward.
The player avoids axe crash, horn charge and ground stomp separately; each failed attempt names the attack and safe response.
Players practice each existing Fade attack from a neutral reset and complete the set without relying on super.
The drill demonstrates why grounded kicks miss, then requires one jump kick and one fireball hit against the flying target.
Each Be'lal pattern can be isolated; success requires surviving its active phase and hitting during its recovery.
Three beam attacks offer valid escape lanes and report whether failure came from late movement or remaining in the beam lane.
A finale sandbox demonstrates shield break, TT readiness and the joint hit without revealing the sequence before the player unlocks it.
The hazard drill alternates two lane warnings and passes after three safe crossings without rewarding standing outside the floor.
A drill compares healing at full and reduced HP and displays recovered versus unused healing amount.
A configurable enemy exposes a known recovery window; the drill scores only hits landing after its active attack ends.
Alternating visible left/right entrances require turning and defending the correct side before a harmless training strike connects.
A melee and ranged target form a bounded exercise with two documented successful solutions and no unavoidable opening damage.
Short existing tell clips ask for the safe response; every answer explains the actual attack lane and remains skippable.

items.improvement: Show personal reaction timing in drills
items.acceptance: A local-only readout measures input delay from a tell onset in simulation time and clearly excludes render/input latency claims.
A read-only demonstration performs the selected lesson with labeled inputs, then hands control back from a fresh reset.

items.improvement: Offer beginner, standard and fast drill variants
items.acceptance: Variants change only practice warning/recovery parameters, label their timing multipliers and leave every original campaign configuration value untouched.

items.improvement: Let players choose an untimed practice goal
items.acceptance: Players may select three successful attempts instead of a timer; waiting or pausing never fails the exercise.

items.improvement: Undo the last practice configuration change
items.acceptance: Undo returns target setup and rule choices to the previous configuration without undoing unrelated accessibility settings.
A stamp records completion of a named lesson without scores, streaks or online identity, and can be cleared from practice.

items.improvement: Suggest a drill from the current session's misses
items.acceptance: With hints enabled, two repeated alignment misses suggest the lane drill once; leaving practice discards the suggestion history.
Clearing practice records requires a clear scope prompt and preserves campaign saves and access settings.
All actions light labeled indicators without damaging a target or spending resources, allowing a new layout to be tried safely.
Slow-play, repeat-kick and aim-assist choices can be tested on a dummy and show their assisted label before a campaign begins.
Five selectable seed cards define fixed practice setups; choosing the same card and settings reproduces target placement.
Players choose up to five already-unlocked drills, restart a single drill, and exit without losing their campaign checkpoint.

items.improvement: Pause demonstrations while instructions are open
items.acceptance: Opening an instruction card freezes its demonstration and resumes the exact move phase when dismissed.
Searching by move name, input or purpose returns the correct existing technique with its current binding and practice shortcut.

items.improvement: Link a defeat explanation to a relevant drill
items.acceptance: A defeat screen can open the matching unlocked practice exercise and return to the same retry checkpoint afterward.

items.improvement: Compare enemy spacing in a training arena
items.acceptance: Players can observe melee-only, ranged-only and mixed spacing presets side by side through selectable setups with no hidden stat changes.
Remix is a separate selection with its own records and clearly identified enemy changes; standard five-stage spawns remain unchanged.
Unlike the existing spear enemy, this remix guard marks a landing spot, vaults across one lane and exposes its back during a fixed landing recovery.
A front-facing shield blocks ordinary frontal kicks but leaves rear and recovery openings; a reference drill proves both counters.
A drummer temporarily speeds nearby allies' decision intervals within a capped radius; defeating it removes the boost on the next tick.
A courier attempts a visible exit after one warning; interception prevents its single reinforcement without affecting stage completion logic.
An arcing projectile has a visible landing marker and can be avoided by lane movement without requiring a jump.
The duelist evades one predictable frontal approach, has a cooldown on evasion and remains punishable from two documented angles.
The mauler commits to a marked swing lane, breaks light cover and gives a longer punish window rather than merely inflated HP.
A distinct harmless feint can precede one real shot; color-independent body cues distinguish them before the commitment deadline.
A support ward protects one visible ally link at a time; breaking the link or displacing the support exposes that ally.
A visible curved projectile travels out and returns once along a shown arc; defeating its thrower cancels the return and every route has a reachable safe lane.
A new small Shadow construct marks its emergence mound for 0.8 seconds, stays underground at most two seconds and cannot emerge beneath an unavoidable hit.
The captain orders one visible formation change at a time; interrupting the order leaves followers using their ordinary AI.
A destructible conduit emits a rotating warning lane and deactivates immediately when broken, including any pending projectile.
Its marked counterstance punishes one repeated approach but expires on a timer and can be baited without unavoidable damage.

items.improvement: Define a shared cue vocabulary for new enemy roles
items.acceptance: All new ranged, support and armored enemies use distinct silhouette symbols shown in their optional practice previews.

items.improvement: Add directional guard resolution for remix
items.acceptance: Front, flank and rear attacks resolve according to a documented angle rule and remain invariant under camera motion.
Shielded remix enemies lose a finite guard reserve from designated moves and show the exact break/recovery state without adding base HP.
A new optional technique reflects eligible small projectiles only during a narrow active window; boss beams and hazards remain ineligible.
Destroying a marked banner cancels only its unspawned reinforcement and never deletes enemies already active in the arena.
A separate remappable move displaces a nearby ordinary enemy with low damage and cannot push a boss outside the arena.
An opt-in move shifts one lane with a cooldown and recovery cost; it cannot be chained into permanent invulnerability.
A distinct airborne input trades forward reach for downward impact and respects existing juggle and landing limits.
Holding the optional charge action has a visible cap and interrupt cost; quick taps retain a documented weaker shot rather than firing twice.
One specified kick may cancel into lane movement by spending meter; the cancel cannot reset attack cooldown or duplicate hit damage.
A short Riley call draws eligible idle enemies toward his last position with a cooldown and never forces bosses or hazards to retarget.

items.improvement: Let remix players choose Loial's entry side
items.acceptance: A clear two-choice preview sets the charge direction before use; cancellation spends nothing and the once-per-stage limit remains.

items.improvement: Add a selectable angreal burst pattern
items.acceptance: Remix offers the existing spread or a short piercing shot, labels the tradeoff and allows only one active pattern per pickup.
A rare clearly shaped token blocks one eligible ordinary hit, expires at stage end and never suppresses taint or the finale rules.
Cover blocks eligible projectiles until broken, has no invisible remaining collision and cannot trap Riley in a lane.
A barrel follows one predictable lane, hits each target at most once and stops safely at arena boundaries.

items.improvement: Add a one-use hanging bell interaction
items.acceptance: A marked bell produces a brief nearby stagger when struck, cannot repeat after activation and never interrupts a cinematic.
A bounded optional patch changes deceleration only after a visible warning; leaving it restores normal traction immediately.
A remix ceiling marker gives a visible countdown before a small stone falls; a safe adjacent lane stays reachable and debris never leaves hidden collision.
Breaking a special crate briefly reduces eligible enemy targeting range while preserving all player-visible attack warnings.
Between remix fights, two clearly marked floor switches open a gate without timers, consumables or a softlock on retry.
A curated wave introduces both sides in staggered groups with a documented safe opening and a bounded concurrent attacker count.
Melee guards protect a slinger while at least one visible route reaches the ranged threat without taking a mandatory hit.
A drummer and supporters demonstrate the benefit of target priority, and clearing either target order always permits progression.
Riley moves a friendly signal marker across one remix arena while enemy hits delay rather than permanently fail the objective.
In remix only, a marked fork predicts one of two charge endpoints and both endpoints leave a reachable counterattack window.
One non-damaging decoy is visually distinguishable by motion and silhouette, and only the real Fade can deal or receive damage.
A visible perch phase creates an anti-air opportunity before a warned dive; the boss remains reachable without rare pickups.
Two visibly different ward phases require alternating safe approaches; neither phase makes all ordinary attacks ineffective indefinitely.

items.improvement: Add a Taim cross-lane volley variant
items.acceptance: A remix volley marks successive lanes and always leaves a reachable gap; the original joint-finish requirement remains intact.

items.improvement: Budget support effects separately in the director
items.acceptance: Only one rally, one ward and one reinforcement order may be active together; queued support cannot starve ordinary enemy turns.

items.improvement: Prevent new attack patterns from eliminating every escape
items.acceptance: A geometry check on curated remix patterns finds a reachable safe corridor before each damage onset using standard Riley speed.

items.improvement: Add an optional remix objective selector
items.acceptance: Players choose survive, interrupt or break-cover objectives with rewards limited to local records and no campaign stat upgrades.

items.improvement: Keep remix tuning in independent configuration
items.acceptance: Changing remix damage, waves or new moves leaves serialized standard five-stage tuning hashes and stage-specific pressure coefficients unchanged.

items.improvement: Deliver a bounded remix balance report
items.acceptance: Forty fixed-seed runs per mode report each existing stage separately, new-role exposure and unavoidable-damage failures; no results replace standard gates.

items.improvement: Add one optional Emond's Field cutscene
items.acceptance: One new skippable 20–35 second scene shows Riley protecting neighbors and a blue dance ribbon clue; skipping preserves all checkpoint rewards.
One new skippable 20–35 second scene uses a street map and Loial's clue to clarify the chase without requiring franchise knowledge.

items.improvement: Add one optional Shadar Logoth cutscene
items.acceptance: One new skippable 20–35 second scene lets Moiraine explain the fog's safe-lane rule through calm action, with no horror close-ups.

items.improvement: Add one optional Stone of Tear cutscene
items.acceptance: One new skippable 20–35 second scene shows TT practicing a brave dance-count rhythm before her existing lightning reveal without changing its payoff.

items.improvement: Add one optional Black Tower cutscene
items.acceptance: One new skippable 20–35 second scene shows the siblings agreeing on a signal before Taim; the existing live joint finish remains playable.
Five named locations unlock in order, explain the current objective in one sentence and hide future story details.
Only cleared chapters are selectable, replays use a separate run slot and the original Continue checkpoint is untouched.
Players can replay only already-seen reels from a named list and return to the same gallery selection afterward.

items.improvement: Remember separately which story scenes were viewed
items.acceptance: Skipping, watching and gallery replay record distinct local states without pretending a skipped scene was fully watched.
Continue can show a skippable two-sentence summary based on the saved stage, Callandor and TT state without revealing the next event.
Riley, TT, Moiraine, Loial and each encountered antagonist receive a short role description gated by first appearance.

items.improvement: Create a place notebook with earned entries
items.acceptance: Each reached location gets one illustrated description and its current relevance; unopened locations remain unnamed placeholders.
Selecting saidin, angreal, Asha'man or Callandor in help opens a short explanation and returns to the exact prior reading position.

items.improvement: Add a current-objective strip between fights
items.acceptance: A one-line inter-wave objective reflects the next arena and disappears before combat cues need the space.

items.improvement: Show explicit reasons for chapter locks
items.acceptance: A locked chapter says which prior stage to clear, never suggests payment and cannot consume a selection input intended for Back.
After each clear, a short card states the achieved goal and next destination while respecting the actual TT and Callandor timeline.
One short non-blocking remark per existing stage adds warmth; it never interrupts an essential warning or delays the next fight.

items.improvement: Give Moiraine a post-retry encouragement pool
items.acceptance: Three brief encouraging text lines rotate without blaming the player and appear only on deliberate retry, not every lost life.

items.improvement: Show TT's dancer identity through an optional keepsake trail
items.acceptance: Five cosmetic blue-ribbon markers, one per existing stage, unlock a single notebook fact each without stats, random drops or required detours.

items.improvement: Add an Emond's Field rescue vignette in scenery
items.acceptance: A background family safely reaches shelter after a cleared wave; the silent event cannot be attacked or mistaken for an enemy.
Three painted signs point to gates, streets and palace consistently with camera progression and remain optional to read.
A quiet safe-area prop group explains why Riley changes lanes without introducing a second new cinematic.
Architectural motifs foreshadow Callandor, remain historically consistent within the stage and do not look like collectible pickups.
Subtle blue cloth signals show a safe route through the grounds and yard without falsely marking hazard lanes as safe.

items.improvement: Give every encounter zone a specific purpose line
items.acceptance: Each of the thirty original zones gets a short optional label explaining what Riley is accomplishing there, with no reused filler label.
The card celebrates finishing and names one skill used, without letter grades, negative labels or comparisons to other players.
Players can inspect their own stage time and resource use with mode and assistance labels; no online comparison or identity is created.

items.improvement: Let players hide scores during the story campaign
items.acceptance: A setting removes score display and results totals while leaving progression, lives and underlying balance unchanged.

items.improvement: Add a story-only viewing route after completion
items.acceptance: Completing the campaign unlocks a sequence of seen reels with no combat and no new story scene assets.

items.improvement: Include a gentle end-of-session stopping point
items.acceptance: At a stage clear, an optional Save and Rest action returns to title with a precise next-stage resume message.

items.improvement: Add a family-readable controls reference sheet
items.acceptance: An offline help page explains one action per line, distinguishes scarce powers and prints legibly on one page.
An optional pre-play page briefly identifies fantasy fights, fog and capture themes without making medical or age-rating claims.
A short art-and-story guide specifies retreat, dazed or dissipating outcomes and is applied to every proposed new enemy concept.
Credits identify existing contributor roles, asset origins and licenses from an offline file without linking to a child's identity.

items.improvement: Create a chapter-by-chapter story continuity sheet
items.acceptance: Every existing and proposed beat lists Riley's goal, TT's location and Callandor ownership; contradictory states are flagged before scripting.

items.improvement: Add a spoiler boundary to help and galleries
items.acceptance: Before the Tear reveal, help, thumbnails and descriptions cannot reveal TT's lightning or Callandor upgrade details.

items.improvement: Let a player mark a seen reel as a favorite
items.acceptance: Favorites store only reel IDs locally, sort predictably and can be removed without altering seen-state or campaign progress.
After the ending, players can preview and locally download a reunion postcard with chosen earned chapter emblems and mode label, with no upload or extra cinematic.

items.improvement: Offer ending credits at the player's pace
items.acceptance: After the existing finale, credits can scroll automatically or page manually, with an always-visible return to title.
In the story gallery only, up to three labeled details per existing painting explain composition or setting without changing the reel.

items.improvement: Add a clear New Run checkpoint warning
items.acceptance: Starting a fresh campaign names the existing saved stage and offers Continue or Replace before overwriting the only active run.

items.improvement: Add a post-clear return route to the chapter map
items.acceptance: After a replayed stage, Return to Chapters restores the map scroll/focus position and does not auto-launch the next story stage.

items.improvement: Provide a bookmark for a story-only viewing session
items.acceptance: The story route resumes at its last finished caption independently of the gameplay save and can be reset alone.

items.improvement: Add choice-free humor to friendly prop descriptions
items.acceptance: Ten optional prop descriptions use kind situational humor, contain no insults about ability and reveal no private family facts.

items.improvement: Make progression rewards explicit at acquisition
items.acceptance: Story cards state that Callandor strengthens the super and that chapter access is unlocked, with each reward acknowledged once.

items.improvement: Offer an optional recap before a boss rematch
items.acceptance: A two-line text recap names the boss's role and Riley's current goal without replaying an entire chapter intro.

items.improvement: Explain the relationship between TT and Kenzie once
items.acceptance: The first notebook entry clearly says Kenzie is Riley's sister and is called Twinkle Toes; later labels remain consistent.

items.improvement: Add a local collectible checklist with no streaks
items.acceptance: The five optional ribbons appear as location silhouettes, never expire and have no daily timer or random rarity.
A read-only notebook view removes unlock masks after campaign completion, keeps action buttons hidden and works entirely offline.

items.improvement: Make added story content individually skippable in settings
items.acceptance: Each of the five optional new scenes can be disabled without suppressing original story beats, rewards or the finale.
Deliver alpha-painted corner, edge, and panel assets that fit the existing HUD rectangles; gameplay screenshots show every current label and value unobscured.
Replace the procedural token artwork with a six-frame blue-white painted token animation; its existing collection radius, lifetime, and healing amount remain identical.
Deliver a six-frame faceted shard animation that reads distinctly from healing and angreal pickups at their existing gameplay sizes; collection behavior is unchanged.
Deliver a recognizable miniature angreal with a six-frame turn; the silhouette remains identifiable at the current pickup size without increasing its collection radius.
Add painted ready and spent Loial medallions beside the existing status text; each uses a different physical design and follows the current availability state.
Show a small painted crystal-sword emblem after the existing acquisition event; screenshots before acquisition, after acquisition, and after Continue show the correct state.
Add a painted reservoir border and transparent interior texture around the existing meter; empty, half-full, and full captures retain the exact current fill widths.
Deliver five boss-specific painted crests for the existing health-bar panel; each appears only for its corresponding boss without changing bar length or displayed health.
Add six painted beads beside the existing wave counter; exactly the completed beads change artwork, and the numeric wave label remains present.

A player explicitly associates profiles using only coarse controller model and reported button/axis capabilities; profiles persist locally, and serial numbers, unique device IDs, fingerprints and device metadata exports or transmissions are excluded.
A player can create, rename and switch among three local mapping profiles for one controller without changing another profile.
A paused calibration panel displays every browser-reported axis and button value while suppressing all gameplay actions.
A measured resting offset of 0.12 produces zero movement after calibration, while full deflection remains reachable.
Each controller profile can select a radial deadzone from 0.05 through 0.40, with continuous normalized movement outside the selected boundary.
A controller reaching only 0.82 at its physical edge can be calibrated to produce full movement without increasing maximum character speed.
An optional profile correction keeps diagonal movement magnitude at or below one for a square-gate controller while preserving cardinal full travel.
Either movement axis can be inverted independently, persists per controller profile, and leaves button mappings unchanged.
Selecting the right stick makes it the movement source while left-stick movement is ignored; switching back restores the previous calibration.
A nonstandard controller can assign any two distinct reported axes to movement and preview both directions before saving.
A controller exposing its directional pad as a hat axis can map all four directions and diagonals without treating its neutral value as movement.
A trigger reported as an axis can bind one action using either a zero-to-one or negative-one-to-one travel range.
A trigger fluctuating around its activation threshold produces one press until it falls below a separately configured release threshold.
An analog button with a weak pressed flag can use a calibrated value threshold, and pressure noise below that threshold never fires its action.
Every button reported by a controller can appear in remapping, including indices above 19, while reserved navigation controls remain protected.
A player can add or remove a second button for an action without replacing its primary button; either button independently activates the same action.
Mapping edits run in a preview copy until Apply; Cancel restores every prior binding and reload never exposes an unfinished edit.
Resetting calibration preserves bindings, and resetting bindings preserves calibration and other saved controller profiles, including after a browser reload.
Switching profiles while a stick or trigger is held produces no newly mapped action until the affected control returns to neutral.
A diagonal stick deflection selects one menu direction using a stable dominant-axis rule rather than moving through two rows or columns.
Holding a directional pad moves once immediately, then repeats after a documented delay; releasing stops repetition before the next update.
Dual-rumble and pulse-only controllers use their supported actuator API, while unsupported or rejected actuator calls leave input responsive.
Twenty impact events in one second produce a bounded haptic schedule, and leaving gameplay cancels pending pulses without a delayed vibration burst.
A player can explicitly preview three strength levels on the selected controller; each preview lasts at most one second and the chosen strength persists locally.
A saved profile referencing absent buttons or axes is flagged before activation, with usable default controls available and the original profile retained.
Players can choose physical-key-code or character-based bindings; changing operating-system keyboard layout affects only the character-based mode.
AZERTY, QWERTZ and Dvorak presets provide distinct documented primary movement and action keys without removing fixed emergency navigation keys.
A keypad digit or Enter can be bound independently from its main-keyboard counterpart in physical-position mode.
Players can add and remove secondary keyboard bindings without changing an action's primary key or silently retaining deleted aliases.
A supported modifier-plus-key chord can map to one action; pressing the unmodified key never triggers that chord and reserved browser shortcuts remain unavailable.
Browser-owned Control or Command shortcuts do not also trigger gameplay actions mapped to their letter keys, including mute and music shortcuts.
Keys received during an input-method composition session neither trigger gameplay nor become stored bindings, and ordinary input resumes after composition ends.
Typing into an in-game profile-name or backup-name field never moves Riley, changes audio settings or activates fullscreen.
A local controls utility shows which keys the browser actually receives during a chosen movement-plus-two-action chord and identifies missing events without claiming to repair hardware.
Before accepting a keyboard binding, the interface lists every primary or secondary binding that would change and supports canceling without mutations.
Three local keyboard profiles retain their mode, aliases and chords independently, and switching profiles updates visible binding labels immediately.
Supported mouse buttons, including exposed side buttons, can map to gameplay actions; browser defaults are suppressed only for buttons the player explicitly binds.
A menu row activates only when pointer press and release occur on that row; dragging away or releasing outside cancels the selection.
Wheel and trackpad deltas navigate supported menu lists in bounded steps, with momentum unable to activate a row or scroll the game page.
A hovering pen highlights the current clickable target without activating it, and the preview clears when the pen leaves the canvas.
In an explicitly selected pen-input mode, simultaneous incidental touch contacts do not activate controls while the pen tip is engaged; normal touch mode remains available.
A physical interaction that emits pointer, touch and compatibility mouse events generates only one action edge across supported event paths.
A connected idle controller no longer overrides keyboard prompts; a genuine controller action switches prompts, while stick drift and pointer movement alone do not.
Concurrent keyboard, stick and touch movement follows one documented ownership rule, never adds beyond maximum speed, and transfers cleanly after the active source releases.
When keyboard and controller both hold an action, releasing either source leaves the action held until the other releases, with only one initial press edge.
Auto, Always and Hardware-only modes control whether combat touch inputs are enabled; a laptop touchscreen does not permanently force touch mode after one tap.
When keyboard movement and controller attacks are used together, relevant prompts can show both active binding families without changing either mapping.
If native fullscreen is unavailable or rejected, a reversible page-filling mode works without a false fullscreen indicator or repeated failed requests.
Browser zoom and mobile browser-chrome changes update the visible canvas rectangle and pointer transform; taps at visible control centers remain aligned without changing world coordinates.
A runtime-readable inventory names every resource required for all five stages, fonts and optional recorded audio, with byte sizes and one release identifier.
After a player requests and completes an offline download, a supported browser can reload and complete all five stages with network access disabled.
Before downloading, the interface shows remaining download bytes and available-storage estimates when supported, and clearly labels unknown estimates.
Interrupting a pack download halfway and restarting it reuses verified completed resources instead of downloading the entire pack again.
The game displays Ready Offline only after every required resource is present and verified; removing one cached required resource clears that status.
A new release uses a staging cache and becomes active only when complete; an interrupted update continues serving the previous complete release.
A prepared update can be deferred until returning to the title screen; receiving an update never reloads an active fight or replaces its resources.
The last complete release remains available for explicit recovery after a failed update, with incompatible newer save formats protected from overwrite.
Reloading the installed game's existing URLs beneath its deployment subpath works offline, while unrelated same-origin pages remain outside its cache handler.
A downloadable self-contained HTML edition includes its code, fonts and assets and completes all five stages from a supported file URL without network requests.
An explicit export downloads a versioned backup containing the player's selected progress and settings, with no network transmission or unrelated browser data.
Selecting a backup displays its game version, checkpoint summary and included settings before any saved state changes, and invalid files produce actionable errors.
An approved restore preserves a recovery copy, writes the replacement atomically, and leaves the original usable if any validation or storage step fails.
The three most recent valid checkpoint generations remain locally selectable with stage and wave summaries, and selecting one requires an explicit restore action.
Changing one payload byte in a saved envelope causes integrity validation to reject it before gameplay reads its contents, without deleting the damaged copy.
Checkpoint ordering uses an incrementing generation rather than wall-clock time, so moving the system clock backward cannot make an older checkpoint replace a newer one.
Interrupting storage at each write step yields either the previous complete checkpoint or the new complete checkpoint on reload, never a partially committed state.
Future schema upgrades run ordered, versioned migrations on a copy and commit only after full validation, retaining the original envelope when a migration fails.
An older game build encountering a newer save schema shows an explanation and export option without resetting, migrating or overwriting that save.
Non-finite numbers, oversized collections and impossible field combinations are rejected at the storage boundary before they can initialize a scene.
When the newest save is invalid, the interface offers valid recovery generations and export of the damaged data instead of silently pretending no progress exists.
If browser storage is unavailable, the game continues with in-memory settings and clearly reports that progress will not survive closing, with local export still usable.
A quota failure distinguishes unsaved progress from a successful save and offers export plus an explicit optional-cache cleanup action without automatically deleting saves.
Ten settings changes inside 200 milliseconds produce one committed settings write, while the final selection survives a subsequent safe scene exit.
The saved indicator appears only after the committed generation can be read back and validated; a failed write instead leaves a visible unsaved state.
Two tabs sharing storage cannot silently overwrite one another's progress; the non-owner can continue temporarily or explicitly take over after a clear warning.
A settings write from another tab is detected and applied only at a safe boundary or explicitly declined, without changing live bindings halfway through a held action.
Returning through browser Back to a cached page restores one active game loop and the existing scene, without duplicate listeners or duplicated audio sources.
On supported page-freeze or pagehide events, an already prepared safe checkpoint is committed once without advancing combat or constructing a partial in-fight snapshot.
After an abnormal close, the next launch identifies the last verified checkpoint and explains what can be recovered, without claiming unsaved combat was preserved.
Session duration uses a monotonic timer; a system clock jump leaves duration nonnegative and marks unreliable calendar timestamps instead of reordering saved progress.

Loss of the main 2D canvas context suspends presentation safely; restoration rebuilds its paint caches and drawing state and resumes unchanged gameplay, independently of the existing puppets.js WebGL mesh-loss fallback.
A fetch or image decode that never settles reaches a bounded timeout and a documented fallback, with no indefinitely blocked loading or scene transition.
Leaving a scene cancels its unneeded pending fetches where supported, and cancelled results cannot install resources into the replacement scene.
A critical script or initialization failure presents a small independent recovery screen with reload and saved-data export paths instead of a permanently blank canvas.
An atlas with out-of-bounds frames or a zero-dimension image is quarantined before drawing and replaced with the existing fallback without crashing the scene.
Where the platform supports verification, mismatched resource bytes are rejected before decode and cannot be marked ready in an offline pack.
A local status panel identifies currently missing or quarantined assets and lets the player retry only those resources without restarting the campaign.
An explicit repair replaces one failed cached resource after verification, retains unaffected cached files, and leaves saves and settings untouched.
Concurrent requests for the same versioned image, JSON or audio resource share one underlying fetch and release references without duplicate downloads.
Each scene disposes its registered timers, event listeners and temporary object URLs on exit; repeated entry and exit does not accumulate live resources.
An asynchronous callback from an exited scene cannot change the current scene, save progress or start audio, even when it resolves after several later transitions.
Decoded optional audio obeys a declared memory budget with reference-aware eviction; active speech and music are never evicted while playing.
Background verification, save preparation and cache maintenance run through cancellable budgeted jobs, with interactive work taking precedence and no job retaining an exited scene.
A spatial index reduces candidate collision checks in crowded encounters while producing the same ordered collision outcomes as the exhaustive reference path.
Movement and collision-query scratch arrays are reused across ticks, remain bounded during a long session, and cannot retain actors after their scene exits.
A visually static title or settings screen stops continuous drawing after settling and redraws promptly on input, animation, asset arrival or viewport change.
Always-on performance bookkeeping uses fixed-capacity numeric buffers without constructing per-frame scene strings or job arrays when detailed inspection is closed.
A repeatedly failing optional visual or haptic subsystem disables itself for the session with a clear status, while critical simulation errors remain visible and trigger safe recovery.
If an incoming scene fails during initialization, its partial resources are disposed and the game returns to a recoverable previous or title state without committing new progress.
A local HTML tool imports a stage definition, edits enemy counts and exports validated JSON without editing runtime files automatically.

items.improvement: Build Docks encounter three around crane cover
items.acceptance: A ranged enemy and movable crate create two viable approaches, and either route completes without spending Loial or super.

items.improvement: Build Docks encounter four as a pier-side defense
items.acceptance: Two staggered groups attack from visible entries while the narrow-looking pier retains the documented full safe movement band.

items.improvement: Build Docks encounter five as a mixed-route test
items.acceptance: Alternating tide gates and support enemies reuse previously taught rules without introducing another hazard immediately before the boss.

items.improvement: Create the Docks boss Harbor Warden
items.acceptance: An original armored Shadow opponent has a clear painted silhouette, non-gory defeat and three attacks based on anchors, lane pressure and recovery.
A floor arc telegraphs a broad close sweep, jumping or retreating avoids it and the anchor recovery exposes the boss for a measured interval.

items.improvement: Implement the Warden's marked mooring pull
items.acceptance: The boss marks one lane before pulling a loose rope barrier across it; the barrier cannot pin Riley against the arena edge.

items.improvement: Implement the Warden's staggered pier slam
items.acceptance: Two sequential impact lanes leave a traversable gap at standard movement speed, and the boss cannot overlay a third simultaneous damage lane.

items.improvement: Add Docks-specific ambience and impact textures
items.acceptance: Optional local water, rope and timber cues match visible events, have non-file fallbacks and remain intelligible under the existing main theme.

items.improvement: Add Docks gameplay text and notebook entry
items.acceptance: A short start objective, three contextual hints and a completion note tell the self-contained story without adding a cinematic reel.

items.improvement: Add Docks checkpoint and retry fixtures
items.acceptance: Each of its six encounters resumes with consistent gate, crane and resource state in a pack-specific save while original saves remain untouched.

items.improvement: Give Docks a separate Normal balance target
items.acceptance: Forty fixed seeds target a 65–85% independent clear rate with three lives and no top-ups; report failures, median damage and duration outside the original five-stage matrix.

items.improvement: Give Docks a separate Hard balance target
items.acceptance: The same forty seeds and controller target a 35–55% independent clear rate on Hard; its result cannot substitute for any original stage's target.

items.improvement: Set a Docks first-play comprehension gate
items.acceptance: A family playtest plan checks tide warning, crane switch and boss counters; mark unrun until actual voluntary players complete it with qualitative notes.
Fixed-seed runs confirm every arena is finishable without a required pickup, Loial or super and resource supply has no deterministic drought across the level.

items.improvement: Set a Docks performance and asset gate
items.acceptance: Cold and warm entries, six encounters and boss effects meet the applicable unchanged engine budgets or remain blocked, with pack-loading cost reported separately.

items.improvement: Add a Docks completion reward without power creep
items.acceptance: Clearing the pack unlocks one local painted postcard and rematch access, with no stat changes carried into the original five stages.

items.improvement: Design Mountains of Mist Trail as the second optional level
items.acceptance: A reviewed six-encounter post-finale route clears a safe mountain pass, avoids another rescue plot and introduces only wind and shelter as new traversal rules.

items.improvement: Paint the mountain ridge and cloud layers
items.acceptance: Original painted ridgelines establish depth without concealing attack silhouettes; static and animated-cloud presentations share the same visible landmarks.

items.improvement: Paint the trail, bridge and sheltered camp
items.acceptance: A continuous six-arena floor depicts apparent cliffs while retaining safe collision boundaries and no lethal falling mechanic.
Wind direction and onset are visible for at least 1.2 seconds, gusts cannot force edge damage and a sheltered lane remains reachable.

items.improvement: Implement shelter stones as a positional tool
items.acceptance: Standing in a visibly marked lee zone removes gust displacement only while inside it; enemies and Riley follow the same rule.

items.improvement: Build Trail encounter one at the lower camp
items.acceptance: A modest melee encounter establishes shelter markings before wind activates, and clearing it opens the upward route without a timed demand.

items.improvement: Build Trail encounter two as a gust introduction
items.acceptance: One gentle gust cycle teaches the safe shelter route with low enemy pressure and no projectile overlapping the first warning.

items.improvement: Build Trail encounter three at the rope bridge
items.acceptance: The bridge is visually narrow but collision-safe; alternating ranged threats leave a reachable lane and never turn knockback into an instant loss.

items.improvement: Build Trail encounter four around shelter choice
items.acceptance: Two shelter areas let Riley choose a safer ranged approach or a faster close route, and both solutions work at standard speed.

items.improvement: Build Trail encounter five as a ridge crossing
items.acceptance: A bounded wind-and-melee sequence combines already-taught rules and provides a quiet recovery interval before the summit boss.

items.improvement: Create the Trail boss Ridge Sentinel
items.acceptance: An original stone-armored Shadow opponent has three wind-and-footwork attacks, a readable painted silhouette and a harmless crumbling defeat.
A marked gust accompanies a slow committed advance; the player can reach shelter or circle behind before damage activates.
Three visibly sequenced stones roll through separate lanes, disappear safely at bounds and leave a route avoidable without jumping.

items.improvement: Implement the Sentinel's summit recoil opening
items.acceptance: After a warned two-part stomp, the boss braces visibly for a fixed recovery window and cannot restart an attack before that window expires.
Optional local ridge wind, rope creak and sheltered hush cues follow the actual gust state without masking essential warnings or requiring network playback.

items.improvement: Add Trail gameplay text and notebook entry
items.acceptance: A start objective, three shelter hints and a completion note explain the new route with no added cinematic or changes to the existing ending.

items.improvement: Add Trail checkpoint and retry fixtures
items.acceptance: Every encounter restores wind phase, shelter layout and resources from its own expansion save; reloading cannot duplicate pickups or boss rewards.

items.improvement: Give Trail a separate Normal balance target
items.acceptance: Forty fixed seeds target a 55–75% independent clear rate with three lives and no top-ups, reported separately from Docks and the original campaign.

items.improvement: Give Trail a separate Hard balance target
items.acceptance: The same forty seeds and controller target a 25–45% independent clear rate on Hard; data stays outside the original five-stage acceptance matrix.
Voluntary playtests must show that shelter markings, safe cliff boundaries and gust direction are understood; no automated run is labeled human evidence.
At minimum HP, maximum gust and edge positions, a reachable legal response avoids every forced-hit chain without rare resources or assisted speed.

items.improvement: Set a Trail performance and asset gate
items.acceptance: All six encounters, cloud layers and three boss patterns meet existing engine limits or are marked unresolved; cold pack-loading costs remain visible.

items.improvement: Add a Trail completion reward without power creep
items.acceptance: Clearing the route unlocks one local summit postcard and rematch access without stronger Riley stats, new accounts or competitive ranking.

items.improvement: Verify expansion isolation from the five-stage campaign
items.acceptance: With either pack enabled or disabled, original seeds, rewards, save migration and Normal/Hard tuning remain unchanged and all five original stages are reported separately.
Each pack has its own evidence, art review, exact candidate and unresolved gates; neither pack ships or modifies the original release without a fresh explicit GO.
